title: The AI Semiconductor Boom and What Could End It with Stacy Rasgon | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 63

metadata.title: The AI Semiconductor Boom and What Could End It with Stacy Rasgon | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 63

summary: Stacy Rasgon describes AI demand spreading from GPUs into CPU, memory, networking and equipment bottlenecks. He upgrades AMD, remains constructive on Broadcom and NVIDIA, and distinguishes Intel's improved narrative from proven manufacturing economics. Eisman owns NVIDIA and endorses the continuing infrastructure cycle. They reject simplistic immediate GPU obsolescence while identifying weak eventual returns and power limits as risks. Later supplier earnings support demand acceleration, but long-horizon revenue, EPS and investment-return claims remain open.
assessment: Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.
speaker_map_notes: Stacy Rasgon supplies technical explanations, analyst ratings and numerical forecasts. Eisman asks questions, discloses NVIDIA ownership and gives the closing endorsement; guest upgrades are not attributed to Eisman.
framework_points: Distinguish earnings revisions from multiple expansion.
Inspect bottlenecks across the entire supply chain.
Treat reported margin changes separately from impairment base effects.
Use GPU rental prices and utilization to assess useful life.
Separate temporary digestion from permanent ROI failure.
Treat management language, warrants and capex announcements as evidence requiring interpretation.
tools_and_charts: SOX forward earnings and P/E decomposition
CPU/GPU rack ratios and agent workload illustration
AMD EPS scenarios and warrant milestones
transcript_cautions: Rasgon corrects Eisman's gross-margin comparison in real time; the correction is preserved.
Rasgon explicitly says fixed CPU/GPU attachment ratios are an imperfect heuristic.
The $600 AMD warrant threshold is a vesting condition, not an unconditional price target.
May 25, 2023 refers to market reaction; the earnings release was the prior evening.
Qualcomm and Intel rumors remain unconfirmed in the extracted claims.

assumptions: Straight-line depreciation, unchanged depreciable cost and residual value, no offsetting impairment.
evidence_basis.proof: Annual expense is depreciable cost divided by useful life. A longer life reduces current expense and increases current pretax profit, while lifetime total depreciation is unchanged. Economic validity requires evidence about useful service life.
